The Dodgers, back-to-back champions in 2024 and 2025, entered 2026 as heavy preseason favorites (roughly 25% implied odds), and I have no reliable information on how their season actually went or on the World Series result. Assuming they are a playoff team in late September, even the strongest team rarely exceeds about 20% to win it all given the randomness of the MLB postseason. Uncertainty about their seeding and health (a first-round bye versus a wild-card series) pulls the estimate slightly below that preseason figure. I therefore put them at about the level of a typical top postseason favorite.

Probability: 0.18

Katie Hobbs is the Democratic incumbent running in a Trump-midterm year, which historically favours the party out of the White House. Arizona remains a closely divided state, and polling I'm aware of through mid-2026 showed Hobbs with only a modest lead over the likely Republican field (Andy Biggs the probable nominee). My knowledge stops in June 2026, so I have no information on the general-election campaign or the result of the 3 November election, and I am forecasting from the pre-election picture. On that basis I rate Hobbs a clear but not overwhelming favourite.

As I recall it, Brent spiked above $100 in spring 2026 on the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, then eased toward the mid-$80s to $90s by early summer on ceasefire and peace-deal hopes. That leaves the $84.99 strike plausibly near the middle of the likely range for August 31, with a slight lean below it if the easing trend continued. With no firm price anchor and only seven trading days of volatility left, I put this close to a coin flip, slightly under.

Abortion-restricting measures have also failed in other red states such as Kansas and Kentucky in 2022. Against that, Missouri is solidly Republican, the measure is bundled with popular-sounding provisions (rape/incest exceptions, parental consent, a ban on gender-affirming care for minors), and it has the governor's backing. I have no reliable result or late polling to draw on, so this is a judgement from those fundamentals, leaning modestly towards the measure failing.

As of my knowledge through mid-2026, Democrats were strong favourites to take the House but underdogs for the Senate, given a difficult map that required flipping several Republican-leaning seats. I don't have the actual election results, so I can't confirm the outcome either way. A sweep with a margin requirement on top of an already unlikely Senate flip puts this at a low probability.
